feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Memadapter: Counterfactual Adaptation Against Memory-induced Sycophancy
entry.summary:
MemAdapter is a novel framework that uses counterfactual reasoning and context-aware reflection to mitigate memory-induced sycophancy in LLM agents without needing to alter or purge valid persistent memories.

Why it matters: It prevents long-term memory systems in LLM agents from forcing uncritical alignment with user bias without requiring aggressive memory filtering.

entry.title: Optimizing the Optimizer: Language Models Discover Faster Molecular Relaxation
entry.summary:
An LLM-based autoresearch agent optimized the open-source Sella molecular geometry optimizer, yielding the AutoSella family that reduces required force-evaluation calls across unseen molecules and potentials.

Why it matters: Automating optimizer code design via language models significantly cuts the computationally expensive force-evaluation calls required for quantum-chemical geometry optimization.

entry.title: In-Distribution Forcing for Long Video Generation at Test Time
entry.summary:
In-Distribution Forcing (ID-Forcing) is a test-time framework that prevents distribution drift in long video generation by using self-caching to construct key-value entries without attending to prior frames.

Why it matters: It enables existing short-horizon autoregressive video diffusion models to generate minute-scale videos without color, texture, or motion degradation, using only test-time interventions.

entry.title: Self-Generated Feedback Destabilizes Test-Time Training: A Causal Decomposition of Long-Horizon Adaptation
entry.summary:
Self-generated feedback during long-horizon test-time training destabilizes model predictions on independent text, a failure causally isolated and mitigated by evaluating updates on independent evidence before retention.

Why it matters: Test-time training on self-generated outputs requires validating updates against independent evidence to prevent model performance degradation over long context windows.

entry.title: Certification of Real Images through Calibrated Content Authentication
entry.summary:
A new deepfake detection paradigm certifies real images by assessing if authenticity is plausibly deniable based on calibrated faithful reconstruction by known generators, remaining robust against adversarial perturbations.

Why it matters: Traditional content-only deepfake detectors are fundamentally unreliable and fragile, whereas reconstruction-based calibrated certification provides a secure method to verify authentic real images despite advancing generative models.

entry.title: SearchJev: A Fast and Calibrated System-1 Model for Search Agents
entry.summary:
SearchJev is a fast System-1 model that directly scores search options without autoregressive generation, using Soft-Label Learning for Calibrated Decisions to handle fast decision-making in search agents.

Why it matters: Separating fast decision-making from generative reasoning significantly reduces search latency and improves calibration while enhancing overall answer accuracy in web-browsing agents.

entry.title: RobotUse: Allocating Computation, Context, and Decisions
entry.summary:
RobotUse is a robot agent harness that separates high-level visual action selection from backend motion planning, utilizing subagents and a persistent playbook to learn from execution.

Why it matters: It enables robot agents to make flexible, context-aware visual decisions while offloading spatial computation and retaining compact execution memories.

entry.title: OmniReasoning: Pushing the Limits of Audio-Visual Joint Reasoning
entry.summary:
OmniReasoning introduces a benchmark, an automated QA data engine, and an on-policy self-distillation method to significantly improve audio-visual joint reasoning in omni-modal models.

Why it matters: It establishes a structured paradigm to prevent omni-modal models from relying on single-modality shortcuts, improving deep cross-modal reasoning in complex video tasks.

entry.title: Noise Out, Bias In: Targeted Bias Injection in Diffusion Language Models via Closed-Loop Activation Steering
entry.summary:
A new targeted bias injection attack uses a proportional-integral (PI) controller to perform closed-loop activation steering across iterative denoising steps in masked diffusion language models.

Why it matters: The attack demonstrates that the iterative denoising trajectory of diffusion language models acts as a controllable attack surface, requiring bias evaluations to audit the active serving stack rather than just the frozen model weights.

entry.title: When to Switch: Reliable Action-Chunk Extension for Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary:
RACE improves Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model performance by predicting subskill transition timing via an auxiliary one-step denoising pass and conditioning action generation on it.

Why it matters: It enables smoother, faster, and more reliable robotic execution by allowing VLA models to use significantly longer action chunks without sacrificing manipulation accuracy.

entry.title: RealtimeWAM: One-Step Asynchronous World Action Models
entry.summary:
RealtimeWAM achieves an end-to-end speedup of up to 25x on an H100 with less than a 1% performance drop using one-step action generation and asynchronous expert execution.

Why it matters: It enables ultra-fast, real-time robotic action prediction from video-based World Action Models without sacrificing execution accuracy.

entry.title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
entry.summary:
Researchers show base language models can achieve RL-level reasoning performance simply by prefixing responses with specific starting token cues derived from associations learned during pretraining.

Why it matters: Understanding that reasoning capabilities can be unlocked via simple prompt cues reduces the necessity of complex reinforcement learning for certain tasks and highlights how pretraining data directly structures model behavior.

entry.title: PerturBot: Breaking Shortcut Priors in Vision-Language-Action Models with Perturbative Training
entry.summary:
PerturBot introduces a training and offline evaluation framework using perturbative data augmentation and GroundingFscore to eliminate modality shortcuts in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models without modifying inference architecture.

Why it matters: It prevents VLA models from failing in novel scenarios by ensuring model scaling reinforces genuine multi-modal task reasoning rather than memorized shortcut correlations.

entry.title: Dynamic Harness Search: Building Multi-Agent Systems Per-Query via Prediction
entry.summary:
SHIFT uses Monte Carlo tree search powered by a local LLM architect and learned value function to dynamically build optimal multi-agent harnesses per query without executing candidates at inference time.

Why it matters: It enables cost-effective, per-query customization of multi-agent workflows without incurring the runtime overhead of executing multiple candidate harnesses during inference.

entry.title: QuantCode Model: Specializing Language Models for Executable Algorithmic Trading Code
entry.summary:
QuantCode specializes LLMs for Backtrader algorithmic trading code generation using framework-specific continued pretraining and agent-validated supervised fine-tuning, evaluated on the new 400-task QuantCode-Bench.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that specialized execution frameworks require both domain pretraining and validated SFT to prevent capability degradation in multi-turn instruction following and tool usage.

entry.title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that base language models can achieve reasoning performance competitive with RL-tuned models simply by prepending specific token cues learned from training data.

Why it matters: It reveals that complex reasoning capabilities in RL-tuned models are largely latent behaviors in base models triggered by specific token associations formed during pretraining.

entry.title: Sharpen Without Search: On-Policy Distillation of Sequence-Level Power Distribution
entry.summary:
On-Policy Power Distillation (OPPD) uses a sequential Monte Carlo sampler to train a language model to directly generate sequence-level power-sharpened distributions, eliminating the need for test-time candidate search.

Why it matters: OPPD enables models to achieve the reasoning performance of computationally expensive multi-candidate power sampling within a single generation step, even without ground-truth reference answers.

entry.title: Balancing Memory Pathways: Analyzing and Improving Memory Utilization in Hybrid LMs
entry.summary:
Hybrid language models over-rely on attention pathways while underutilizing recurrent states, but an auxiliary loss restricting attention access forces better dual-memory pathway coordination and improves long-context task performance.

Why it matters: Architectural access to complementary memory systems is insufficient; models require explicit training objectives to prevent attention mechanisms from bottlenecking recurrent state utilization.

entry.title: You Changed Your Mind, The Model Didn't: Demystifying Intent in Multi-Turn Dialogue
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Intent-Eval to benchmark language model performance under changing user intent and proposed Intent-OPSD, an on-policy self-distillation framework that mitigates performance degradation caused by mentioned-as-in-effect confusion.

Why it matters: Multi-turn conversational AI systems frequently fail when users alter or retract requirements, making intent-tracking frameworks like Intent-OPSD essential for reliable execution in dynamic workflows.

entry.title: Multimodal Safety Evaluation Should Measure Controllability Beyond Classification
entry.summary:
A new multimodal safety evaluation framework introduces controllability profiles using sparse feature decompositions to measure internal representation-level detectability, intervention sensitivity, and benign-preserving selectivity.

Why it matters: Future VLM safety benchmarks must measure whether safety-relevant internal signals can be controlled without damaging benign capability, rather than relying solely on classification accuracy.

entry.title: The Assistance Dilemma: Learning to Teach via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
The Eduardo multi-turn RL training recipe introduces a masked near-transfer post-test and binary reward gates to train LLMs into effective tutors without resorting to answer-telling.

Why it matters: It enables smaller language models to match frontier-model tutoring benchmarks while significantly reducing latency and token costs for real-time interactive teaching.

entry.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
entry.summary:
A new framework for looped language models introduces learned depth priors and orthogonal input injection, improving performance while enabling efficient truncated backpropagation, terminal KV sharing, fast prefill, and accelerated RL updates.

Why it matters: These optimizations significantly reduce the computational and memory overhead of looped language models across training, decoding, prefill, and reinforcement learning without sacrificing model accuracy.

entry.title: How Sparse Probability Maps Shape Mixture-of-Experts Routing
entry.summary:
A study on top-2 MoE models reveals that sparse probability maps like entmax, sparsemax, and normmax co-adapt with learned score distributions during training, failing to lower validation loss but significantly boosting inference-time K-scaling robustness.

Why it matters: Adaptive MoE routing must be engineered around the co-adapted interaction between the probability map and learned score distributions rather than the map's theoretical sparsity alone.

entry.title: Learning What to Imitate: Entropy-Aware Distribution Mixing
entry.summary:
Entropy-Aware Mixing dynamically interpolates student and teacher distributions based on the student's predictive entropy to prevent confident conflicts and performance degradation during language model distillation.

Why it matters: It stabilizes knowledge distillation to improve mathematical reasoning in small language models while mitigating catastrophic forgetting of general capabilities.

entry.title: What Matters for Latent Reasoning with Flow Matching
entry.summary:
Flow-based Latent Reasoning (FLaRe) introduces a flow matching training recipe in learned latent space that enables language models to reason continuously across five key criteria: usefulness, diversity, explainability, refinability, and efficiency.

Why it matters: FLaRe demonstrates that flow matching in continuous latent spaces can match explicit step-by-step reasoning performance at a fraction of the computational latency.

entry.title: Does Learning Protein Folding Generalize to Broader Reasoning?
entry.summary:
Fold2Reason uses protein structure data to post-train language models, yielding improvements on protein structure prediction and transferring gains to broader spatial, scientific, and general reasoning tasks.

Why it matters: Non-linguistic, structure-dense scientific data can serve as an effective post-training supervision source to improve general model reasoning beyond the target domain.

entry.title: FrameMorrow: Future-guided Frame Selection with Prospective Tokens for Long-Horizon Video Generation
entry.summary:
FrameMorrow introduces a prospective frame selector that predicts compact tokens representing future information needs to select relevant historical frames for long-horizon video generation.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, memory-efficient long-video generation by selecting key history based on future requirements without needing access to internal model weights.

entry.title: MotorMind: Scaffolding General Vision Language Models for Zero-Shot Robot Manipulation
entry.summary:
MotorMind is a robot manipulation harness that enables general vision-language models to perform zero-shot manipulation by mapping VLM-proposed mid-level actions to deterministic control with asynchronous monitoring and background memory updates.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that general-purpose VLMs can perform effective real-world robotic control without complex external tooling, task-specific training, or specialized policy networks.

entry.title: World Action Modeling with Progressive Visual Planning
entry.summary:
ProWAM is a world action model that improves robotic control by jointly predicting action sequences and an ordered sequence of sparse visual sub-goals, caching sub-goal features to eliminate iterative full-video generation during replanning.

Why it matters: By decoupling sparse visual planning from dense action denoising, ProWAM enables efficient, robust long-horizon robotic control and strong zero-shot real-world generalization.

entry.title: On-Policy Parameter Update Direction Underlies Generalization in LLM Post-Training
entry.summary:
Researchers show that on-policy post-training generalization stems from its dynamically adjusted cumulative parameter update direction, which can be transferred to Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to improve generalization.

Why it matters: By constraining SFT to on-policy update directions, developers can combine the superior generalization of on-policy post-training with the high computational efficiency and trajectory utilization of SFT.

entry.title: Native Action-Prior Learning from Videos for World Action Models
entry.summary:
NAVA-WAM introduces native action-prior learning, directly pretraining an Action-DiT policy on observation-only videos using future-video flow-matching supervision before post-training on action-labeled robot data.

Why it matters: It enables scalable robot policy pretraining directly from vast, unannotated video datasets without requiring expensive action labels or complex latent-action grounding.

entry.title: Pivot-SD: Efficient Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Pivot-SD is an offline self-distillation framework for masked diffusion language models that selectively trains high-impact commitment tokens (pivots) identified via an information-gain metric.

Why it matters: It improves post-training efficiency and benchmark performance for masked diffusion language models by targeting individual trajectory-shaping tokens instead of updating entire sequences or denoising steps.

entry.title: SimuVerity: Benchmarking Agents for Engineering-Grade Simulink Model Generation
entry.summary:
SimuVerity is a new benchmark containing 101 text-to-executable Simulink generation tasks that evaluates AI agents against engineering specifications rather than simple compilation or structural similarity.

Why it matters: It establishes a rigorous, specification-driven standard for evaluating whether AI agents can generate functionally correct, production-grade control and dynamic systems in Simulink.

entry.title: HyperBrowseComp: A Multilingual and Multimodal Stress Test for Web-Browsing Agents
entry.summary:
HyperBrowseComp is a new multilingual and multimodal web-browsing benchmark featuring 423 manually authored, human-validated questions across 13 languages designed to stress-test AI agent information-seeking capabilities.

Why it matters: It establishes a rigorous benchmark to evaluate how effectively autonomous agents navigate complex, multi-step clue chains and diverse media across non-English web environments.

entry.title: Source Preference in the Wild: How LLM Agents Favor Items by Source, and How to Reduce It
entry.summary:
Evaluations of 12 LLM search agents across three domains reveal strong source preference bias, where models frequently select inferior items from favored sources over better-fitting items from dispreferred sources.

Why it matters: Source bias in LLM agents can distort fair market competition and undermine search accuracy by steering users toward sub-optimal choices based solely on brand or domain identity.

entry.title: Science or Slop?: Benchmarking and Mitigating Scientific Slop in AI-Generated Papers
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced SciSlopBench to measure AI-generated scientific slop via global reasoning metrics, and developed SciSlopHarness to mitigate these structural flaws using grounded experiment records.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that AI-generated scientific papers harbor global reasoning failures invisible to standard token detectors, providing a framework to accurately identify and ground synthetic research writing in empirical data.

entry.title: LexReward: A Taxonomy-Driven Reward Framework for Legal Language Models
entry.summary:
LexReward is a taxonomy-driven legal reward modeling framework that evaluates language model outputs across three distinct dimensions: Style, Element, and Chain.

Why it matters: It replaces coarse holistic judgments with fine-grained, interpretable legal reward signals that explicitly improve policy outputs in style, factual accuracy, and reasoning chain structure.

entry.title: Spatial Memory Intelligence: Endowing World Models with Understanding-Driven Long-Term Memory
entry.summary:
Spatial Memory Intelligence (SMI) uses a multimodal large language model to systematically manage spatial memory in long-video world models via four coordinated atomic operations.

Why it matters: It improves long-video generation stability and spatial consistency in world models by replacing unmanaged history with intelligent, MLLM-driven memory pruning and retrieval.

entry.title: Science Utopia? Closed-Loop LLM Simulation of Academic Research Ecosystems
entry.summary:
SciUtopia is a persistent, closed-loop LLM-agent simulation framework that models multi-year academic research ecosystems, including peer review, funding, collaboration, and researcher attrition.

Why it matters: It provides a configurable testbed for conducting counterfactual experiments and targeted interventions on scientific funding, review mechanisms, and research policy.

entry.title: EditHero: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Part-Level 3D Editing and Vibe Modeling
entry.summary:
EditHero is the first benchmark for long-horizon, part-level 3D editing featuring natural-language instructions, target images, and a deterministic assembly engine for geometry and texture.

Why it matters: It establishes a rigorous framework for evaluating multi-step 3D asset revision, highlighting code-generating AI agents as a superior approach for localized, non-destructive mesh editing.

entry.title: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Frontier Reasoning Data Synthesis
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced task-harness co-evolution, a recursive harness self-improvement framework that dynamically adapts generation workflows and skills alongside synthesized reasoning problems to continuously generate harder benchmarks.

Why it matters: Updating the data synthesis harness itself alongside task generation produces significantly harder reasoning datasets that directly enhance downstream model fine-tuning.

entry.title: OptiSelect: How does the Optimizer Shape Data Curriculum?
entry.summary:
OptiSelect formalizes optimizer-aware online data selection for LLM pretraining, proving theoretically and empirically that diagonal-adaptive optimizers like AdamW and Sophia provide superior selection gain over sign-based preconditioners like Lion and Muon.

Why it matters: It provides theoretical foundations and practical co-design rules for selecting data scoring geometries that maximize training efficiency in large language model pretraining.

entry.title: IDRF: Inverse-Distilled Reward Fine-tuning of Masked Discrete Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
IDRF enables reward fine-tuning for few-step masked discrete diffusion models by replacing the intractable sequence-level KL divergence with an inverse-distillation loss.

Why it matters: IDRF allows masked discrete diffusion models to undergo efficient reward alignment and maintain sample quality at significantly lower sampling latency.

entry.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation
entry.summary:
A theoretical and empirical study proving that the choice of divergence objective in distillation acts as an implicit entropy regularizer, with forward KL inflating student entropy and reverse KL deflating it.

Why it matters: Understanding how different divergence functions implicitly control student entropy enables principled selection of distillation objectives for model compression, pretraining, and finetuning.

entry.title: Metropolis-Hastings Dominates Importance Resampling for Policy Composition
entry.summary:
Researchers prove that independence Metropolis-Hastings achieves lower sampling bias than sampling-importance-resampling for decoding-time LLM policy composition across all rollout budgets and convex f-divergences.

Why it matters: It establishes Metropolis-Hastings as a mathematically superior inference-time method for adjusting multi-reward trade-offs in LLMs without costly retraining.

entry.title: KV$^2$: A Self-Refining KV Cache
entry.summary:
KV$^2$ is a query-agnostic KV-cache compression method that reduces memory footprint by using a lightweight proxy scorer to filter tokens before selectively reprocessing only the most informative subset to compute eviction scores.

Why it matters: It enables efficient long-context model serving in multi-query settings by significantly reducing KV-cache memory costs without the high computational overhead of full-context reprocessing.

entry.title: Gains and Collapse in On-Policy Distillation:A Reinforcement Learning Perspective
entry.summary:
Framing on-policy distillation as reinforcement learning reveals that performance gains and length-collapse stem from teacher implicit rewards amplifying student behaviors, rather than expanding student capabilities.

Why it matters: Understanding OPD as implicit reward learning shifts the optimization focus from teacher generation quality to teacher evaluation reliability, providing concrete methods to prevent length collapse during model post-training.

entry.title: Emergent Structure in the Marginal Attention Space of Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers analyzed the post-softmax marginal attention space across 60+ LLMs, discovering a text-intrinsic token signature linked to input-output Jacobians and a model-private head signature useful for static KV cache budgeting.

Why it matters: It enables efficient KV cache eviction by decoupling static, model-specific head budget allocation from dynamic, text-intrinsic token scoring.

entry.title: The Geometry of Knowledge Accessibility in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Knowledge accessibility in LLMs has a geometric structure in the query's pre-generation representation space, where accessibility decreases with distance from a central point, forming a knowledge boundary that dictates effective inference interventions.

Why it matters: This pre-generation geometric signal enables adaptive inference frameworks to dynamically select the most effective intervention (such as rewriting, chain-of-thought, or retrieval) before generating a response.

entry.title: HyperThink: Text-to-Parameter Hypernetworks for Efficient Reasoning
entry.summary:
HyperThink uses a lightweight text-to-parameter hypernetwork with a vector-quantized decoder to predict base LLM parameter updates, replacing long inference-time thinking traces with a single query-conditioned forward pass.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces sequential decoding latency and token consumption in LLMs while maintaining strong multi-step reasoning performance.

entry.title: Memorizon: Training World Models Beyond Their Context Window
entry.summary:
Memorizon trains streaming world models on ultra-long spans by decoupling supervision length from attention sequence length using a co-visibility-retrieved latent bank.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, long-horizon training for world models to maintain consistent scene generation during revisits without exploding computational costs.

entry.title: RLE-Bench: A Qualifying Exam for Coding Agents as Robot Learning Engineers
entry.summary:
RLE-Bench is a benchmark designed to evaluate coding agents across full robot learning engineering workflows rather than isolated control policies.

Why it matters: It establishes a systematic framework to measure and improve how autonomous coding agents handle complex, multimodal, real-world robotics development tasks.

entry.title: Generalization Is Stability, Not Accuracy: Multi-Axis Evaluation of LLMs
entry.summary:
A new framework, Stability-Aware Generalization Objective (SAGO), evaluates LLM generalization by measuring individual example variability across multiple input variants rather than relying on aggregate benchmark accuracy.

Why it matters: Measuring performance via aggregate accuracy hides model fragility, whereas multi-axis stability evaluation prevents misleading benchmark rankings caused by narrow prompt optimization.

entry.title: Devils in Question Relay: Source-Conditioned Relay Steering to Mitigate Hallucinations in Audio-visual Large Language Models
entry.summary:
SECRET is a training-free method that mitigates source-confused grounding hallucinations in Audio-visual Large Language Models by steering question states toward required-source evidence.

Why it matters: It provides an inference-time solution to cross-modal interference in AVLLMs, improving reliability in multimodal reasoning without requiring model retraining.

entry.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
entry.summary:
KaliBench is a dataset and benchmark of 8,504 natural-language-to-CLI query-command pairs across 1,642 Kali Linux tools, providing runtime-free verifiable rewards for training and evaluating LLM tool execution.

Why it matters: It provides deterministic, runtime-free reward signals to train small open-weight language models to accurately execute complex CLI commands for real-world cybersecurity operations without runtime overhead.

entry.title: JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces
entry.summary:
JevSpawn is a compositional, training-free policy that connects natural language task specifications to finite probabilistic exploration using parallel action spawning and feedback-driven branch selection.

Why it matters: It enables faster, computationally efficient LLM agent navigation and execution without requiring additional model training or predefined action spaces.

entry.title: MemFold: Learning Compact Soft Memory for Long-Context Personalization via On-Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
MemFold introduces a method to compress query-conditioned textual memories into K continuous soft-memory vectors using on-policy optimization with group-relative rewards and confidence-gated distillation from a frozen teacher.

Why it matters: It enables long-context personalization with bounded input length by training soft memory components directly on the downstream model's behavior rather than text reconstruction.

entry.title: When Does Correction Become Repair? Mechanistic Auditing of Internal Interventions in Tool-Using LLMs
entry.summary:
The SAKIKO framework audit-mechanizes internal steering in tool-using LLMs, proving aggregate gain metrics can obscure severe collateral corruption of baseline-correct decisions.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard aggregate metrics are insufficient to validate activation steering, requiring outcome-resolved adjudication to prevent undetected corruptions in tool-using agentic models.

entry.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
entry.summary:
A cheap diagnostic ladder reveals that keyword-matching benchmarks mask tool-use failures in small models, which can be localized via first-token probes and fixed using targeted, low-compute SFT.

Why it matters: Lenient keyword-based benchmarks allow broken tool-use models to pass as functional, requiring stricter diagnostic gating before deploying small language models.

entry.title: Before It Fades: Reinforcing Temporal Representations at Inference Time in VideoLLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Temporal Activation Injection (TAI), a training-free inference method that prevents video language models from losing temporal information by reinjecting the temporal divergence vector from intermediate layers into later layers.

Why it matters: TAI fixes a core failure mode in VideoLLMs—insensitivity to temporal order—at inference time without requiring expensive model retraining.

entry.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
TACO is a memory-efficient optimizer that computes the exact steepest-descent direction under a dimension-normalized 1-to-1 operator norm by selecting the ternary sign of each weight matrix column's largest entry.

Why it matters: TACO drastically cuts optimizer memory overhead, enabling full-parameter fine-tuning of 30B+ parameter LLMs on a single GPU without compromising accuracy.

entry.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Mathematical Primitives, the diagnosis benchmark HLEI, and ABS, a primitive-privileged self-distillation framework that repairs reasoning failures and improves LLM mathematical performance across scales.

Why it matters: Identifying specific mathematical bottlenecks allows targeted post-training distillation frameworks to significantly improve LLM reasoning capabilities without relying solely on overall solution accuracy metrics.

entry.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
ZFO decouples direction and step-size selection in LLM fine-tuning by using first-order optimizers for direction and lightweight zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size.

Why it matters: It offers an adaptive, lightweight step-size selection mechanism that stabilizes and speeds up large language model optimization without the heavy overhead of traditional line searches.

entry.title: Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free
entry.summary:
LoopCD is a training-free contrastive decoding framework for looped Transformers that contrasts final recurrent predictions with earlier intermediate states to improve output accuracy while reducing inference compute.

Why it matters: It enables significantly higher accuracy and up to 48.2% lower inference FLOPs in parameter-efficient looped Transformers without requiring additional model training.

entry.title: Learn the Directions, Normalize the Gains: Post-Training Normalization for LoRA
entry.summary:
LoRA-Norm is a post-training method that addresses adaptation imbalance by applying spectral rebalancing and nuclear-norm restoration to learned LoRA updates without needing calibration data, extra training, or inference overhead.

Why it matters: It provides a zero-overhead post-training fix to preserve general model capabilities during LoRA specialization without requiring retraining or calibration datasets.

entry.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
entry.summary:
DMAD replaces auxiliary score fitting in distribution matching distillation with an adversarial framework using two discriminator heads to directly learn log-density ratios for fast, few-step visual generation.

Why it matters: DMAD significantly reduces memory and compute costs during diffusion model distillation while achieving state-of-the-art visual quality in few-step image, video, and audio-video generation.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust Schrödinger Bridge
entry.summary:
Distributionally Robust Schrödinger Bridge (DRSB) introduces a single-controller formulation that minimizes worst-case control energy and target KL penalty under initial distribution shifts.

Why it matters: It enables stochastic transport models, such as image-to-image translation, to reliably reach target distributions even when input data experiences out-of-distribution shifts at test time.

entry.title: Exploring Weaknesses of Generative Image Watermarks against Latent Frequency Masking
entry.summary:
Latent Frequency Masking is a new attack that erases invisible generative image watermarks by replacing Fourier coefficients in the image's latent representation using Gaussian noise or diffusion regeneration.

Why it matters: It reveals latent-frequency manipulation as a critical attack surface that watermark developers must account for in future robustness evaluations.

entry.title: Counting Moves, Weighing Voices: Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation for Calibrated Multi-LLM Councils under Persistent Adversaries
entry.summary:
Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation (BDA) models typed multi-LLM deliberation moves to estimate per-agent reliability, enabling calibrated posterior confidence and robustness against persistent adversaries without additional LLM calls.

Why it matters: It enables multi-LLM councils to produce accurate, well-calibrated confidence scores and maintain decision integrity even when under attack by persistent adversarial coalitions.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Alignment for Decoder-Only Models using MoE Routers
entry.summary:
A novel cross-lingual alignment method applies contrastive learning directly to mixture-of-experts (MoE) router outputs instead of hidden states in decoder-only LLMs.

Why it matters: It enables effective cross-lingual representation alignment in modern decoder-only MoE architectures, leading to enhanced cross-lingual transfer and multilingual performance.

entry.title: MoLE: Mixture of Latent Experts for Complementary Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
MoLE is a Mixture of Latent Experts framework for vision-language models that isolates latent visual experts during evidence extraction and aggregates them with summary experts to prevent redundant representations.

Why it matters: Specializing latent token computation produces diverse, non-redundant visual reasoning states that outperform simply increasing the total number of latent tokens.

entry.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
entry.summary:
NEPA introduces Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression and Multi-Embedding Prediction to dynamically update condition embeddings at every denoising step of a DiT, achieving 1.32 FID on ImageNet 256x256 with lower training compute.

Why it matters: Dynamic state-aware embedding predictions significantly reduce the training compute needed for high-quality image generation in diffusion transformers.

entry.title: Universal interpolation for deep residual self-attention networks
entry.summary:
Deep residual softmax self-attention networks with fixed, Gaussian-initialized projection matrices achieve universal interpolation of token sequences purely through sequence depth and layer selection, without scaling width or re-training parameters.

Why it matters: It proves that deep transformer models like Looped Transformers can achieve universal function approximation using tiny, fixed parameter sets executed sequentially rather than requiring massive wide architectures.

entry.title: SIEVE: Selective attention-value Suppression for Vision-Language Models Unlearning
entry.summary:
SIEVE is a selective unlearning framework for vision-language models that suppresses attention-value representations to zero for forget targets while matching retain representations against a frozen reference model.

Why it matters: It enables vision-language models to selectively erase sensitive personal data associated with a visual identity without destroying permitted knowledge about the same individual.

entry.title: Do Your Own Research: Learning to Forecast by Learning to Search
entry.summary:
A new framework trains a language model using single-epoch GRPO and Brier-score rewards to actively search, filter, and gather its own evidence before forecasting real-world outcomes.

Why it matters: Allowing reinforcement learning rewards to directly shape an agent's search and evidence-gathering behavior produces superior forecasting accuracy at a fraction of frontier model inference costs.

entry.title: On-Policy or Off-Policy Learning? A Systematic Study of Distillation Dynamics
entry.summary:
A controlled study on Llama3 and Qwen2.5 shows rollout policy is less critical than token-level KL direction for task performance, while learning rate drives forgetting and update sparsity.

Why it matters: The findings challenge the assumption that on-policy rollouts are inherently superior, helping practitioners optimize distillation pipelines by prioritizing KL direction and learning rates over complex policy data generation.

entry.title: Transformers Stop Thinking Too Early, and a Tiny LoRA Fixes It
entry.summary:
A task-trained rank-8 LoRA applied to a single early layer enables frozen pretrained transformers to process significantly longer in-context reference chains by initiating a hidden state relay across middle layers.

Why it matters: A minimal, single-layer parameter edit unlocks deep contextual reasoning capabilities that remain latent and underutilized in default pretrained transformers.

entry.title: Video Generation Models: A Survey of Post-Training and Alignment
entry.summary:
This survey provides the first comprehensive review of post-training and alignment techniques in video generation models, categorizing them into a taxonomy of implicit and explicit alignment across four methodological paradigms.

Why it matters: It offers a structured framework to adapt pretrained video models for improved controllability, temporal consistency, and safety without requiring full retraining from scratch.

entry.title: Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free
entry.summary:
LoopCD is a training-free contrastive decoding framework for looped Transformers that uses intermediate recurrent states as guidance to improve inference quality while reducing compute.

Why it matters: It improves LLM reasoning performance and significantly cuts inference FLOPs for parameter-efficient looped architectures without requiring additional model training.

entry.title: Persona Dosing: Calibrated Activation Steering for Graded Trait Control
entry.summary:
PersonaDose introduces calibrated activation steering to control language model persona traits by specializing a shared FLAS controller and calibrating flow time against measured trait intensity.

Why it matters: It enables precise, graded behavioral control over language model traits using calibrated intensity requests rather than uncalibrated steering coefficients.

entry.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
entry.summary:
Where-OPD is an on-policy self-distillation method for MLLMs where a teacher model receives privileged textual spatial guidance from procedurally generated synthetic scenes, enhancing student perception without external models or human annotations.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that synthetic, spatially guided self-distillation transfers effectively to real-world visual perception and reasoning tasks without requiring costly human annotations.

entry.title: Better Supervision Is Nearby: Neighborhood On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
Neighborhood On-Policy Self-Distillation (N-OPSD) improves mathematical reasoning models by using local parameter perturbations to create a pool of frozen expert teachers that supervise student-sampled prefixes.

Why it matters: N-OPSD extracts stronger, position-specific supervision from parameter perturbations during training without adding memory or compute overhead at inference time.

entry.title: Ego2Act: Evaluating Goal-Directed Manipulation in Egocentric Video Generation
entry.summary:
Ego2Act is a new benchmark featuring 2,640 egocentric videos across 110 real-world tasks to evaluate goal-directed, multi-step physical manipulation in video generation models.

Why it matters: It establishes a rigorous framework to benchmark whether video generation models can function as physically plausible world simulators for embodied planning and AI robotics.

entry.title: VTR-Bench: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Text Rendering in Video Generation
entry.summary:
VTR-Bench evaluates visual text rendering in video generation models across 300 prompts and five scenarios, introducing an automated evaluation pipeline and a Keyframe-Guided Agentic Framework to iteratively refine generated output.

Why it matters: It exposes a critical failure mode in current video generation models and provides a standardized benchmark and agentic workflow to improve in-scene text accuracy.

entry.title: AgSpec: Pushing the Limits of Retrieval-Based Speculative Decoding in Coding Agent Pipelines
entry.summary:
AgSpec improves retrieval-based speculative decoding in coding agents by retrieving from session, workspace, and global corpora while dynamically managing draft lengths through offline profiling and online feedback.

Why it matters: It significantly accelerates inference speeds for LLM-based coding agents without requiring extra neural draft models, reducing pipeline latency and cost.

entry.title: SemanTok: Predictable Semantic Tokens for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
entry.summary:
SemanTok is a flexible video tokenizer that feeds frozen DINO features into its encoder and uses lightweight heads to reconstruct semantic features directly from retained token prefixes.

Why it matters: It improves autoregressive video generation efficiency and fidelity by enabling smaller models to achieve performance superior to significantly larger baselines using shorter token prefixes.

entry.title: Removing the NEEDLE in the Haystack: Backdoor Removal in LLMs via Weight Orthogonalisation
entry.summary:
NEEDLE is a training-free backdoor removal method for LLMs that uses activation vectors and sequential weight orthogonalisation to eliminate triggers without degrading safety or general capabilities.

Why it matters: It enables post-hoc mitigation of LLM backdoor attacks without requiring retraining, clean baseline models, or sacrificing general model safety and utility.

entry.title: DataMagic: Authoring Data Videos through Declarative Multi-Agent Orchestration
entry.summary:
DataMagic generates data videos from raw tabular data using a declarative specification (DVSpec) and a multi-agent orchestration framework that optimizes narrative coherence.

Why it matters: It enables automated, data-accurate video generation from raw tabular inputs while significantly reducing manual editing time and cognitive effort.

entry.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
entry.summary:
ScholarCatalyst is a benchmark based on annotations from 184 lead authors evaluating model ability to retrieve literature that inspired their recent computer science papers.

Why it matters: It establishes a benchmark proving that current AI agents and search techniques lack the expert intuition required to navigate broad literature archives and locate foundational ideas for new research.

entry.title: LOCI: Spatial Linear Memory for Streaming World Models
entry.summary:
LOCI is a hybrid spatial-memory world model architecture that combines a visual key-value cache with a recurrent linear-attention memory conditioned on projective camera geometry for streaming video synthesis.

Why it matters: LOCI allows streaming video world models to maintain spatial memory consistency when revisiting locations while operating within a fixed GPU memory budget.

entry.title: Asynchronous LLM Post-Training: Group-Mass Capping and Convergence Analysis
entry.summary:
Group Mass Capping GRPO (GMC-GRPO) mitigates stale-rollout bias in asynchronous LLM post-training, reducing the fourth-order delay term's threshold dependence from O(ε⁻⁴) to O(ε⁻²).

Why it matters: GMC-GRPO enables stable, efficient asynchronous RL post-training for LLMs under heavy rollout delays without persistent clipping bias.

entry.title: Universal Byte-Level Encoding: UTF-8/UTF-16 Routing to Reduce Cross-Script Token-Budget Disparities
entry.summary:
Universal Byte-Level Encoding (UBE) routes 1-2-byte UTF-8 characters through UTF-8 and 3-4-byte characters through UTF-16 before BPE to reduce token-budget disparities across scripts without compromising English efficiency or decoding accuracy.

Why it matters: UBE reduces cross-lingual token cost inequities and expands usable context window sizes in multilingual LLMs without altering core BPE algorithms or degrading performance in English.

entry.title: Same Reward, Different Skills: When Multimodal RL Learns to Look
entry.summary:
Researchers show that standard RLVR induces visual grounding skills only when tasks enforce visual resolvability, requiring visual evidence for success rather than allowing shortcuts through text or language-only heuristics.

Why it matters: To build truly grounded multimodal models, benchmark and RL task designs must require visual information to solve the problem rather than relying solely on text-based correctness rewards.

entry.title: GAW-PO: Preference Optimization with Gradient-Aligned Token Weights
entry.summary:
GAW-PO improves Direct Preference Optimization by reweighting rejected tokens based on gradient alignment with preferred updates, preventing useful tokens in rejected responses from being unfairly penalized.

Why it matters: It provides effective token-level credit assignment in preference tuning, preventing models from degrading when aggressively optimized using lower β values.

entry.title: No Model Required: Text Entropy Rate Filtering Mitigates Iterative Fine-Tuning Collapse
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a non-parametric text entropy rate estimator, Kontoyiannis $h_k$, that mitigates model collapse during iterative fine-tuning on synthetic data without requiring model log-probabilities, external oracles, or human data.

Why it matters: It enables model-agnostic, computationally efficient training-data filtering that preserves text diversity and prevents model degradation across successive generations of synthetic fine-tuning.

entry.title: Gacha Decoding: Eliciting Diverse Generations Through Instruction Following
entry.summary:
Gacha Decoding is an inference-time method that replaces token entropy sampling with instruction-following and external random number generation to improve language model output diversity.

Why it matters: It enables developers to extract significantly more diverse, high-quality outputs and discover novel response modes from capable language models while drastically reducing the required sample count.

entry.title: FERPO: Forward Entropy-Regularized Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
Forward Entropy-Regularized Policy Optimization (FERPO) is an on-policy maximum entropy RL algorithm that updates actors using critic values directly, avoiding action-derivative critic gradients.

Why it matters: FERPO avoids unreliable policy updates caused by inaccurate critic action-derivatives while offering faster execution and better multi-modal exploration in continuous control tasks.

entry.title: SoftServe: A Scalable Quasi-Newton Method for Deep Learning
entry.summary:
SoftServe is a scalable quasi-Newton optimization method using variational curvature estimates and coupled Newton-Schulz iterations to handle non-convexity and high parameter counts without line searches.

Why it matters: SoftServe makes second-order optimization practical for massive, ill-conditioned neural networks by eliminating costly matrix decompositions and ad hoc curvature fixes.

entry.title: Local Support Learning
entry.summary:
Local Support Learning (LSL) prevents catastrophic forgetting in large pre-trained models without using prior data by pairing weight adapters with Gaussian Mixture Model gating functions that restrict updates to local input activation distributions.

Why it matters: LSL enables continual post-training of 7B-parameter LLMs while preserving past capabilities without the compute and storage overhead of retaining prior dataset copies.

entry.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
entry.summary:
Where-OPD uses on-policy self-distillation with synthetic scenes, providing MLLM teachers with textual spatial coordinates to train students without human annotations or external models.

Why it matters: It proves that synthetic, spatially guided self-distillation enables scalable MLLM post-training that transfers effectively to real-world visual perception without relying on human annotations or larger teacher models.
